verses.text: Soon after this, Jesus travelled through towns and villages, preaching and telling the good news of the kingdom of God. The twelve were with him,
and so were some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses. One was Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.
Another was Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod's manager. There was also Susanna, and many others. These women used their own money to support Jesus and his followers.
A large crowd gathered, and people came to him from every town. Then he told this story.
"A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the path. It was trampled on, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
Some fell on rock. As soon as it grew, it dried up, because it had no moisture.
Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew up with it and choked it.
And some fell on good soil. It grew and produced a crop a hundred times as much." When he had said this, he called out, "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!"
His followers asked him, "What does this story mean?"
He said, "You have been given the chance to know the secrets of the kingdom of God. But to others I speak in stories, so that, 'They may look but not see, and hear but not understand.'
This is what the story means. The seed is the word of God.
The seed along the path stands for people who hear, but then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so that they will not believe and be saved.
The seed on the rock stands for people who hear the word and receive it with joy. But they have no root. They believe for a while, and when testing comes they fall away.
The seed that fell among thorns stands for people who hear, but as they go on their way they are choked by worries, riches, and the pleasures of life. Their fruit never grows ripe.
But the seed on good soil stands for people with an honest and good heart. They hear the word, hold it tight, and by keeping on they produce a crop.
No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a bowl or puts it under a bed. They put it on a stand, so that people who come in can see the light.
Nothing is hidden that will not be shown, and nothing is secret that will not be known and come into the light.
So be careful how you listen. Whoever has will be given more. Whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away."
Jesus's mother and brothers came to him, but they could not get near him because of the crowd.
Someone told him, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you."
He answered, "My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it."
One day Jesus got into a boat with his followers and said to them, "Let us go over to the other side of the lake." So they set out.
As they sailed, he fell asleep. A storm of wind came down on the lake, and the boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
The followers went and woke him. "Master, Master, we are going to die!" they said. He woke up and spoke firmly to the wind and the raging water. They stopped, and it was calm.
"Where is your faith?" he asked them. Afraid and amazed, they said to one another, "Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him!"
They sailed to the area of the Gadarenes, which is across the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, a man from the town met him. This man had been controlled by demons for a long time. He wore no clothes and did not live in a house, but in the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before him, and shouted, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!"

Jesus had commanded the evil spirit to come out of the man. Many times the spirit had seized him. He was kept under guard and bound with chains and shackles, but he broke the chains, and the demon drove him into the desert.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "Legion," he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
They begged Jesus not to order them to go into the deep pit.
A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. The demons begged Jesus to let them go into the pigs, and he let them.
The demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
When the men who looked after the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and told it in the town and in the countryside.
People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone, sitting at Jesus's feet, dressed and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the man who had been controlled by demons was healed.
Then all the people of the area of the Gadarenes asked Jesus to leave them, because they were very afraid. So he got into the boat and went back.
The man from whom the demons had gone begged to go with him. But Jesus sent him away and said,
"Go back home and tell what great things God has done for you." So the man went through the whole town, telling what great things Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, because they were all waiting for him.
Then a man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus's feet and begged him to come to his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around him.
A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all she had on doctors, and no one could heal her.
She came up behind Jesus and touched the edge of his coat. Straight away her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, "Who touched me?" Everyone denied it. Peter and those with him said, "Master, the crowds are crowding and pushing against you, and you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But Jesus said, "Someone did touch me. I know that power has gone out from me."
When the woman saw that she could not hide, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of all the people she told why she had touched him, and how she had been healed straight away.
He said to her, "Daughter, take heart. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace."
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader's house and said, "Your daughter is dead. Do not bother the Teacher any more."
But Jesus heard it and said, "Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed."
When he arrived at the house, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said, "Do not weep. She is not dead. She is sleeping."
They laughed at him, because they knew she was dead.
But he sent them all outside. He took her by the hand and called, "Child, get up!"
Her spirit returned, and she got up straight away. He told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were amazed, but he ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
